title: Geometric-fibre open-immersion criterion with flat source
statement: Let $S,X,Y$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $f:X\to Y$ an $S$-morphism. Assume $X\to S$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], $Y\to S$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and $f$ is locally of finite presentation. For every geometric point $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$, with $\Omega$ algebraically closed, form $f_{\bar s}:X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ using scheme fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-geometric-point]. If every $f_{\bar s}$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], then $f$ is an open immersion. If every $f_{\bar s}$ is an isomorphism, then $f$ is an isomorphism. In particular both tests apply to a locally finitely presented map between smooth $S$-schemes [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Empty schemes and empty fibres are allowed, and no reducedness or Noetherian assumption on $S$ is imposed.

source.place: Stacks Tag 039E (lemma-morphism-between-flat), with morphisms.tex Tag 02GM (lemma-etale-flat-etale-fibres) and etale.tex Tag 025G (theorem-etale-radicial-open). This is their geometric-fibre criterion consequence: fibrewise flatness gives flatness, and geometric fibres of f are empty or a single reduced point, giving etale and universally injective; surjectivity gives the isomorphism clause.

proof.text: Fix $s\in S$ and an algebraic closure $k=\kappa(s)\subset\Omega$. By [lem-pc-field-extension-fpqc-cover], $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is an fpqc cover; by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering-axioms] its pullback $Y_s\times_k\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y_s$ is an fpqc cover. The universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies the pullback of $f_s:X_s\to Y_s$ along this cover with $f_{\bar s}$: both sources classify pairs consisting of an $X$-point and an $\Omega$-point with the same $S$-image, and the projections agree. The hypothesis makes this map an open immersion, so [lem-galois-fpqc-descend-open-immersion] makes $f_s$ an open immersion. This works for every $s$, including empty fibres.

An open immersion identifies its source with an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion]. Its local-ring maps at source points are therefore isomorphisms. Such an isomorphism makes the target local ring a free module of rank one over the source local ring, hence flat. Thus every $f_s$ is flat in the stalkwise sense [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-flat-fibre-test] at each $x\in X$: its hypotheses are precisely that $X\to S$ is flat and locally of finite presentation and $Y\to S$ is locally of finite type. Since $f_s$ is flat at the point over $x$, that criterion says $f$ is flat at $x$. Hence $f$ is flat.

Fix $y\in Y$, choose $\Omega=\overline{\kappa(y)}$, and let $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ be the corresponding geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. Compose it with $Y\to S$ to obtain $\bar s$. By the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product], the geometric fibre $X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ of $f$ is $X_{\bar s}\times_{Y_{\bar s}}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, with the same projection to $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$: both classify an $X$-point and an $\Omega$-point whose $Y$-images agree. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] it is an open subscheme of $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. The only opens of this one-point scheme are the empty scheme and the whole scheme, so its structural map is respectively the empty map or the identity. Each is unramified by [def-weil-unramified-morphism]: it is locally of finite type and its diagonal is an identity on the source, hence an open immersion. A finite polynomial presentation is in particular a finite generating set, so local finite presentation of $f$ implies local finite type [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Consequently [lem-trf-geometric-fibre-unramified-criterion] applies and proves $f$ unramified.

Let $K$ be any field and let $a,b:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$ satisfy $f a=f b$. Choose an algebraic closure $K\subset\Omega$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and write $r:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}K$. The pairs $(a r,1)$ and $(b r,1)$ give maps into $X_{\bar s}$, where $\bar s$ is their common composite to $S$, and have the same image in $Y_{\bar s}$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. An open immersion is an isomorphism onto an open subscheme, so maps into its source with the same composite are equal [def-weil-open-immersion]. Thus $a r=b r$. The singleton $\{r\}$ is an fpqc cover [lem-pc-field-extension-fpqc-cover]. Apply the uniqueness assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] to the common restriction $a r=b r$ (its compatibility follows because it is the restriction of $a$). It gives $a=b$. The field-point criterion in [def-weil-radicial-morphism] now proves $f$ radicial.

We have proved flatness and unramifiedness, and local finite presentation of $f$ is assumed. Thus $f$ is etale by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Together with radiciality, [lem-weil-pbc-radicial-etale-open] proves that $f$ is an open immersion.

Under the stronger hypothesis that every $f_{\bar s}$ is an isomorphism, each is an open immersion by the open-subscheme definition [def-weil-open-immersion], so the preceding argument applies. For any $y\in Y$, take $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(y)}\to Y$ and its composite $\bar s$ to $S$ [def-weil-geometric-point]. The map $(\bar y,1):\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(y)}\to Y_{\bar s}$ lifts along $f_{\bar s}^{-1}$ to $X_{\bar s}$. Projection to $X$ gives a point mapping to $y$, by the projection equations [def-pc-fibre-product]. Thus $f$ is surjective on points. An open immersion identifies $X$ with an open subscheme $U$ of $Y$; surjectivity gives $U=Y$, and the same identification is an isomorphism $X\simeq Y$.

source.place: Tag 025G, conclusion for a surjective open immersion

proof.text: If $X$ and $Y$ are smooth over $S$, [lem-pc-smooth-flat] gives that both structure morphisms are flat and locally of finite presentation. A finitely presented algebra is finitely generated by its displayed polynomial variables, so $Y\to S$ is locally of finite type [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The assumed locally finitely presented map $f$ therefore satisfies all the hypotheses already used. No step required reducedness, Noetherianity, quasi-compactness or nonempty fibres; if $Y$ is empty the isomorphism assertion is vacuous and its open-subscheme identification still gives an isomorphism.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q115-cd4319063 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and all 7 steps in full; the delivery adds no new nodes, the statement is unchanged, and no fixes were needed. The statement is EGA IV 17.9.5 in the form of Stacks 039E+02GM+025G. I checked the hypotheses against more-morphisms.tex l.4682 (039E) and etale.tex l.1370 (025G). Step 1: X_s×_{Y_s}(Y_s×_kΩ)=X×_SΩ; fpqc descent of open immersions (02L3) then makes every ordinary fibre f_s an open immersion. Step 2: open immersions are flat, and the relative fibre flatness test (039E) gives f flat. Step 3: the geometric fibre of f at ȳ is the base change of f_{s̄}, hence open in the one-point Spec Ω, so it is empty or all of Spec Ω and in both cases unramified; 02G8 applied over Y gives f unramified. Step 4: open immersions are monomorphisms, so ar=br, and fpqc uniqueness (023Q) gives a=b, so f is radicial (01S4). Step 5: f is étale and radicial, so it is an open immersion (025G). Step 6: surjectivity follows by lifting (ȳ,1) through f_{s̄}^{-1}. Step 7: smooth gives flat and lfp. Edge cases I checked: empty source and empty fibres, id over a nonreduced base, and Spec k→Spec k[ε] (excluded by the flatness hypothesis). Duplicate search found no node with this statement; lem-pe-flat-lfp-monomorphism-open and lem-sfb-space-etale-monomorphism-open are alternative tools, not duplicates. Batch-5 check: lem-trf-localization-finite-presentation-ring-map (reached through lem-sfb-relative-flat-fibre-test) is pure commutative algebra, and lem-trf-geometric-fibre-unramified-criterion is Stacks 02G8. Neither is a step in the proof of the trace formula or of Poincaré duality, so both citations are accepted. The route is unchanged and no SGA source is used. The 6 declared generic tool_uses are accepted.
